knowledge_point.title: Finding the Augmented Matrix of a System of Linear Equations

question.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-1x+y+z &=-1 \\ x+z &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x+y+z &=-1 \\ x+0y+z &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z &=1 \\ 0x-y-z &=-1 \\ x+y+0z &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-1x+1y &=-1 \\ -1z-1y-1 &=-1x \\ z+1x &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x+y+0z &=-1 \\ x-y-z &=1 \\ x+0y+z &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}1x-1y &=1 \\ 1z+1y+1 &=1x \\ z-1x &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $x,y,z$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+0z &=1 \\ -x+y+z &=-1 \\ -x+0y+z &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
